Reasoning: The answer key states three distinct morphologies across the panel set: LHCE-plated Li is flat, smooth and dense; commercial electrolyte gives dendritic Li; ILE gives nodular Li. Critically, at least one panel (or pair of panels) in this six-panel set must show a flat, smooth, dense morphology corresponding to LHCE. However, the candidate's independent descriptions characterize every single panel (a through f) as rough, textured, granular, porous, mesh-like, or bumpy — none is described as flat, smooth, or dense. This uniformly rough/porous characterization directly contradicts the key's requirement that one condition (LHCE) appear flat, smooth and dense. While isolated keywords like "dendritic" (panels a and f) and "nodular/granular" (panel c) loosely echo two of the three expected morphologies, the complete absence of any smooth/dense/flat panel — replaced instead by rough/granular/porous language everywhere — constitutes a contradiction of a core, specific feature the key attributes to this panel set, not merely an omission.
